docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Default protective order (standing order, June 1, 2017)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Default protective order (standing order, June 1, 2017): In complex cases (patent, trade secret, securities fraud are the examples) where the parties believe a protective order is needed, the court’s default order applies until a stipulated or contested order is entered. Material may be designated “Confidential Pursuant to the Court’s Default PO” and then only outside counsel and the court and its personnel may access it. His survey answer says to execute a protective order sooner rather than later.

docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Patent page limits (standing order, June 3, 2021)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Patent page limits (standing order, June 3, 2021): Absent prior approval in exceptional circumstances: summary judgment 30 pages total moving, 30 opposition, 10 reply; Daubert motions 20 moving, 20 opposition, 5 reply; each motion in limine 5 pages. Survey: he follows L.R. 16.6, enters a scheduling order through Markman and a second through summary judgment, and asks parties to rank disputed terms by importance for the hearing. A technical tutorial is usually allowed.

docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Scheduling and case management (survey)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Scheduling and case management (survey): He does not as a rule convene in-person scheduling conferences. The court issues a scheduling order after the parties’ suggestions, with a date near the end of fact discovery to report whether both sides want the court’s mediation program. Status conferences are rare; written status reports may be requested. Be ready to address mediation, willingness to proceed before the magistrate judge, and expert use. Sizeable class discovery or an MDL is the circumstance in which he would bifurcate discovery.

docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Discovery (survey)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Discovery (survey): He typically resolves discovery motions himself, on the papers and without a hearing, and a party may ask for a shortened response period inside its filing. He expects good-faith best efforts to produce all appropriate discovery. Experts are limited at trial to their reports. Treating physicians are not treated as experts and may produce their records early instead of a Rule 26 report. He sets no Daubert deadline.

docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Dispositive motions (survey)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Dispositive motions (survey): Absent pre-approval in exceptional circumstances, one summary judgment motion of no more than 30 pages. Replies only with leave of court, and 10 pages or less. No hearing on a motion to dismiss unless the papers suggest one would help. Same for summary judgment, and he will entertain a request to hold it by Zoom.

docs.t: Judge Richard G. Stearns (D. Mass.) — Trial practice (survey)
docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Trial practice (survey): A trial brief is required in civil and criminal cases. Proposed voir dire, instructions, witness and exhibit lists, and motions in limine are due two weeks before trial; he prefers instructions in Word-accessible form. No page limit on motions in limine, and he typically rules on them in advance except in bench trials. Courtesy copies of trial exhibits are due one week before trial in the form they will be offered. Agreed exhibits are pre-marked numerically, objected-to exhibits by letter. Civil openings are typically limited to 25 minutes and closings to 45, with strict limits for trials over a week. He seats 8 civil jurors, allows no attorney voir dire, and holds no sidebar conferences during trial.

docs.t: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni (D. Mass.) — Posted standing orders
docs.x: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni, D. Mass.. Posted standing orders: Confidentiality agreements (August 12, 2014): parties are encouraged to sign confidentiality agreements that will facilitate discovery and must file any such agreement that covers discovery. The court takes notice of the agreement but does not adopt it as an order. A dispute is decided on a motion, weighing the agreement with other factors, and Rule 26(c) relief remains available in extraordinary circumstances. His survey says protective orders are discouraged absent special circumstances. Motions for default judgment: after a notice of default, the movant must follow Rule 55, file damages affidavits, and submit a form of default judgment. The defaulted party has 14 days to file a substantiated opposition and ask for a hearing. The court rules on the papers after that period. The motion is due within 30 days of the order (14 da

docs.t: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni (D. Mass.) — Scheduling and discovery (survey)
docs.x: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni, D. Mass.. Scheduling and discovery (survey): Springfield scheduling conferences are held before the magistrate judge, who also handles discovery issues, so the survey routes most pretrial questions there. He typically refers discovery motions to the magistrate judge and holds no discovery hearing. He holds status conferences 3 to 4 months before trial for trial issues, including motions in limine, evidentiary matters, trial length, witnesses, and realistic settlement prospects. Daubert motions are scheduled 3 to 4 months before trial at the final pretrial conference. With pro se litigants he relaxes technical and deadline standards slightly, but only until the litigant has fair notice that the usual standard applies.

docs.t: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni (D. Mass.) — Dispositive motions (survey)
docs.x: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni, D. Mass.. Dispositive motions (survey): No courtesy copies of exhibits. Reply briefs are allowed on request for good cause, with a page limit that depends on the issues. He often holds hearings on motions to dismiss and summary judgment, with generally no time limits, though he may ask counsel to move on or wrap up. He may request a short page-limited brief on an unanticipated issue after argument and will consider requests to supplement on narrowly identified issues.

docs.t: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni (D. Mass.) — Trial practice (survey)
docs.x: Judge Mark G. Mastroianni, D. Mass.. Trial practice (survey): No trial brief unless there is a demonstrated need from complexity. Deadlines for voir dire, instructions, witness and exhibit lists, and motions in limine come in a scheduling order about 7 to 10 weeks before trial, with motions in limine due earlier. He often hears motions in limine at the final pretrial conference but reserves many for trial. No courtesy copies of trial exhibits. Exhibits are pre-marked in coordination with the Clerk. Jury instructions are requested by the midpoint of trial, with a chance to supplement. Time limits for civil trials go in the pretrial order. Jurors write notes on general questions and are then interviewed outside the courtroom by the judge and attorneys, and attorney voir dire is allowed on that basis. A jury questionnaire request must be filed by the motion in limine deadline. He seats 9 ci

docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Each defendant must give the plaintiff a written response to its settlement proposal at least seven days before the conference. The joint statement must also include a concise summary of each side’s position on liability and relief sought. Parties must say whether all consent to a magistrate judge for all purposes and, if so, jointly file the consent form. In an ordinarily complex case, propose a schedule that finishes fact discovery, expert discovery, and pretrial motions within one calendar year of the conference. docs.t: Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) — Form scheduling order
docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Form scheduling order: Her form order sets initial disclosures, a cutoff for amending pleadings, interim fact discovery deadlines, a status conference near the close of fact discovery (status report due two days before), expert designation and deposition dates, and a summary judgment filing date, with oppositions due 21 days after service. Replies need no leave if they are at most 8 pages double-spaced and filed within 7 days after the opposition. Anything else needs leave. Extension motions must give the original dates, prior requests and results, reasons, the other side’s position, and the discovery remaining, and must be made at least 48 hours before the deadline absent an emergency. docs.t: Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) — Discovery and dispositive motions (survey)
docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Discovery and dispositive motions (survey): She usually resolves discovery motions herself, sometimes referring them to a magistrate judge, and holds a hearing only if the dispute is complex or she has questions. Emergency discovery motions are entertained rarely, and only in true emergencies. Counsel should meaningfully confer before dispositive motions. On summary judgment, the opposing party should put its response under each fact in the movant’s concise statement so the fact and response are in one document. No courtesy copies by default, though she sometimes orders them by docket order. She typically allows replies and will allow surreplies if warranted, often with page limits. She usually holds hearings on motions to dismiss and summary judgment, sets no time limits, and often grants short post-hearing supplemental briefs if leave is given at the heari

docs.t: Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) — Trial practice (survey)
docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Trial practice (survey): A trial brief is required. The initial civil pretrial conference sets the trial date, trial length and practices, and mediation interest, with nothing to file in advance. Pretrial deadlines back out from the final pretrial conference and fall one to two months before trial. Stipulated exhibits should be pre-marked, and courtesy copies of trial exhibits are required. She prefers to resolve Daubert motions before the final pretrial conference. Trial days run 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. and she meets counsel each morning at 8:30 to resolve anticipated evidentiary disputes. She seats 10 civil jurors and rarely allows attorney voir dire. Slide decks at motion hearings should be used sparingly, if at all. She typically conducts status and initial scheduling conferences by Zoom.

Memoranda limited to 25 pages, replies to 10, unless permission is granted; 10 pages or more needs a table of contents. Courtesy copies are not required.

docs.t: Judge Frederic Block (E.D.N.Y.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Frederic Block, E.D.N.Y.. Oral argument: Request it by letter when filing the fully briefed motion; the court decides and sets the date and time. Motions are returnable as counsel is notified.

docs.t: Judge Frederic Block (E.D.N.Y.) — Communications and adjournments
docs.x: Judge Frederic Block, E.D.N.Y.. Communications and adjournments: Letters copied to all counsel; no copies of counsel’s correspondence. Calls to chambers are permitted, including to ask about a pending motion or flag time concerns; scheduling and docketing to the courtroom deputy at (718) 613-2425. Faxes only with prior authorization. Adjournment and extension requests must be in writing, state the original date, number of prior requests and their outcome, and the adversary’s position with reasons, and propose revised dates if others are affected. Requests to adjourn appearances are due 48 hours ahead, absent an emergency.

docs.t: Judge Frederic Block (E.D.N.Y.) — Joint pretrial order
docs.x: Judge Frederic Block, E.D.N.Y.. Joint pretrial order: Required only if the court so decides at the initial pretrial conference. Contents: caption; trial counsel; jurisdiction statements with statutes and citizenship facts; claims and defenses to be tried (and those dropped); jury or bench and trial days; magistrate consent (without naming parties); stipulations; witnesses (in person or by deposition); deposition designations; and exhibit lists. Exhibit lists should cover only what parties expect to present and are final at least 1 week before trial. Star any substantive objection; unstarred exhibits are deemed admitted at the start of trial, and meritless authenticity or foundation objections may draw sanctions. Premark exhibits and exchange them at least 10 days before trial; the court needs no copies.

docs.x: Judge Frederic Block, E.D.N.Y.. Pretrial filings (trap): Due 15 days before trial (or 30 days after the final pretrial order if no trial date): a detailed damages statement by claim, in bench cases a statement of elements with supporting facts, motions in limine, and an optional pretrial memorandum. In jury cases, requests to charge and voir dire are listed as due the Thursday before trial (the rules list this under the 15-day heading). Charge requests should cover only the elements, damages, and defenses; the court prepares general instructions.

docs.x: Judge Gary R. Brown, E.D.N.Y.. Pre-motion letters (trap): Before any motion returnable before Judge Brown, file a letter of 2 to 4 pages requesting a pre-motion conference. The court sets the response deadline, which is also the deadline for cross-motion letters. The letters, Rule 56.1 statements, and argument at the conference may be treated as the motion itself, and arguments not raised there are deemed waived. For Rule 12(a), Rule 56(b), and 28 U.S.C. § 1447(c) timing, the letter counts as the motion. No letter needed for IFP, habeas, Rule 50, 52, 59, or 60 motions, reconsideration, orders to show cause, extensions of time to appeal, objections to reports and recommendations, Social Security and bankruptcy appeals, and default judgments or unopposed petitions to confirm arbitration awards.

The opponent files a letter response and a 56.1 response that reproduces each paragraph with its response and citations directly beneath; failure may mean facts deemed admitted or the motion granted. The movant answers any additional paragraphs within 7 days in the same format.

docs.x: Judge Gary R. Brown, E.D.N.Y.. Meet and confer under Local Civil Rule 37.3(a) first; without certification the magistrate judge may deny the motion. Motions to dismiss, for summary judgment, to change venue, to remand, for default judgment, and to confirm arbitration awards go to Judge Brown.

The forms’ fee tables list presumptive maximum hourly rates of about $110 for paralegals, $100–295 for associates, and $200–375 for partners (footnote numbers run into the figures in the PDF text).

docs.x: Judge Gary R. Brown, E.D.N.Y.. docs.x: Judge Gary R. Brown, E.D.N.Y.. docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. In criminal cases, sentencing submissions over 50 pages go to the court in hard copy at the same time as filing.

docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Filing, sealing, and chambers: Filings are due by 5:00 p.m. Eastern on the deadline day and must be text-searchable where practicable. Chambers reviews ECF filings the first business day after submission; call chambers if something needs immediate attention. Sealing is two-step: move for leave with a cover letter explaining the need and the document itself (for redactions, both versions or the unredacted version with proposed redactions highlighted). If granted, re-file under the correct ECF event; if denied, file publicly or not at all. Audio/video exhibits too large for ECF may not be submitted on USB or CD; contact chambers for instructions and file a cover letter on ECF. Proposed orders and jury instructions also go to chambers in Word (WordPerfect acceptable), but not stipulations of dismissal or settlement unless requested. All communications by lett

docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Adjournments and extensions: In writing, stating the original date, number of prior requests, whether they were granted, and whether the adversary consents (and its reasons if not), with proposed revised dates for any affected deadlines. Make requests at least two working days before the appearance or deadline absent an emergency; a request to adjourn an appearance within 24 hours of it also requires a phone call to chambers. In criminal cases, two business days (five for sentencing).

docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Joint pretrial order: Due within 60 days of the close of discovery unless ordered otherwise, prepared under the supervision of the magistrate judge on that judge’s schedule, in a uniform font. Meritless authenticity or chain-of-custody objections may draw sanctions. Also list each motion in limine the party intends to file, with a brief description.

docs.t: Judge Pamela K. Chen (E.D.N.Y.) — Trial filings
docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Trial filings: Motions in limine are due 14 days before trial. In jury cases, requests to charge, proposed verdict sheets, and voir dire are due the Wednesday before trial. Submit one joint charge document limited to elements, damages, and defenses, showing each side’s version where there is no agreement, plus Word files.

docs.t: Judge Pamela K. Chen (E.D.N.Y.) — Criminal sentencing
docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Criminal sentencing: Defense sentencing applications are due at least 5 business days before sentencing; the government’s response or other applications at least 2 business days before.

docs.x: Judge Pamela K. Chen, E.D.N.Y.. Younger lawyers and pronouns: The court strongly encourages less experienced attorneys to argue, present, and examine witnesses at every stage. Parties may tell the court (in writing or through the courtroom deputy) their preferred pronouns or honorifics, and all must use them for each other.

Private mediation or the court’s mediation program does not count; the conference must be in person or by video (not telephone), parties with full settlement authority must attend without exception, and written settlement proposals must be exchanged beforehand. docs.x: Judge Nusrat Choudhury, E.D.N.Y.. Trial procedures: Jury trials run Monday through Thursday, 10 am to 4:30 pm, with counsel time from 9:00 to 10 am and lunch 12:30 to 1:30 pm. Bring two copies of documents used on direct for the court and one each for the reporter and opposing counsel; counsel keep custody of original exhibits. docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Briefing and motion papers (trap): No bundling rule: file motion papers promptly, not when fully briefed. No courtesy copies. docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Summary judgment (trap): The motion may be denied for nonconforming Rule 56.1 statements. docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Filing and ECF: Every request for relief, letter or motion, is filed as a “motion” on ECF, and every entry must describe its subject (not just “Letter”). Amended complaints must attach a PDF redline against the prior complaint. Affidavits of service are prohibited except for the summons and complaint (and in pro se cases); ECF filing is service. In § 2254 cases each part of the state court record must be labeled separately on ECF, or it will be rejected.

docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Chambers communications and adjournments: Communicate by ECF letter, with copies to pro se parties; no hard copies of letters to chambers. Civil adjournment and extension requests are by ECF letter stating the original date, prior requests and outcomes, each side’s reasons for and against, all scheduled dates with an agreed modified schedule, and the grounds; consent alone is not a sufficient ground. docs.t: Judge Brian Cogan (E.D.N.Y.) — Case management plan
docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Case management plan: The judge’s Civil Case Management Plan form sets non-expert discovery cutoffs (not adjourned without good cause), lets parties extend interim deadlines by consent if the cutoff holds, and requires a damages attachment for money claims. The pre-motion letter for dispositive motions is due one week after non-expert discovery closes; there are no cross-motions, and late motions wait until the timely motion is decided. Requests to change plan dates need a proposed order showing all counsel’s positions and affected dates.

docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Civil pretrial and trial: All civil matters except pro se cases, including pretrial matters, are heard by Judge Cogan, not a magistrate judge, absent a referral or consent. The form requires witness and exhibit tables with objections and their bases, precise deposition designations, and exhibits pre-marked in order of use (plaintiff numerals, defendant letters). Do not overdesignate; “reservations” to call more witnesses have no effect. Deliver objected-to exhibits and testimony to chambers when the order is filed. At the start of trial, give the courtroom deputy, in duplicate, a complete set of documentary exhibits, an exhibit list, and the witness list.

docs.t: Judge Brian Cogan (E.D.N.Y.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Brian Cogan, E.D.N.Y.. Criminal cases: No pre-motion letter is needed; argument on all criminal motions is heard on a date the court sets. Multi-defendant filings must name only the defendants they concern. A guilty plea to a supervised-release violation requires 24 hours’ notice specifying the violations. Defense sentencing adjournment requests are due 5 business days ahead, the government’s response 2 business days before. docs.x: Judge Karen M. Williams, D.N.J.. Witnesses and exhibits: She prefers live witnesses and may allow remote testimony for good cause if no one objects. docs.t: Judge Karen M. Williams (D.N.J.) — Jury

docs.t: Judge Karen M. Williams (D.N.J.) — Criminal

docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — Pre-motion letter
docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. Motion days and argument: The return date only sets the briefing schedule. Argument isn’t generally heard on it, and the court will tell counsel if it wants argument.

docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — Adjournments
docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. Summary judgment: Follow the same pre-motion procedure first. docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — Filing and copies

docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. Chambers: Don’t call with questions the rules answer. No fax or email. All communications with chambers are letters filed on CM/ECF, with no hard copies. Docketing and scheduling questions go to the courtroom deputy between 9:00 and 4:00.

docs.t: Judge Renée Marie Bumb (D.N.J.) — RICO and class actions
docs.x: Judge Renée Marie Bumb, D.N.J.. RICO and class actions: File a RICO case statement within 30 days of the complaint under Appendix O. In class actions she holds a preliminary settlement approval hearing and expects you to address the Rule 23(e), Girsh, and Prudential factors.

docs.x: Judge Edward S. Kiel, D.N.J.. Motion day: The return date sets the briefing schedule. Motions are decided on the papers with no appearance unless notified.

docs.t: Judge Roy Altman (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Roy Altman, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Email is the preferred way to reach chambers. The judge has no standing order, so follow the Federal Rules, the Local Rules, and every administrative order in the case. Chambers won’t answer substantive questions or ones the rules already cover, and you shouldn’t call for the status of a motion or case. docs.t: Judge Jacqueline Becerra (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Jacqueline Becerra, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Use the chambers email address, which is the preferred method, and copy all opposing counsel or pro se parties on every message. Chambers won’t answer substantive questions or ones the rules already cover.

docs.t: Judge Beth Bloom (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Beth Bloom, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Counsel can contact chambers, including the deputy and law clerks, about her procedures and hearing scheduling, but not substantive matters or questions the rules cover. Copy all opposing counsel on every email to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Beth Bloom (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Beth Bloom, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: Counsel must appear in person for hearings on all substantive motions. To appear by phone, move at least one day before the hearing, and use a landline.

docs.t: Judge Beth Bloom (S.D. Fla.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Beth Bloom, S.D. Fla.. Settlement: If a case settles, contact chambers immediately and file a notice of settlement.

docs.t: Judge Beth Bloom (S.D. Fla.) — Sentencing
docs.x: Judge Beth Bloom, S.D. Fla.. Sentencing: If a sentencing hearing will run over 30 minutes, tell the courtroom deputy at least 7 days ahead.

docs.t: Judge Beth Bloom (S.D. Fla.) — Civil scheduling order
docs.x: Judge Beth Bloom, S.D. Fla.. Civil scheduling order: Her sample civil scheduling order has proposed orders and proposed jury instructions and verdict forms emailed to chambers in Word format, and requires a mediation report.

docs.t: Judge Darrin P. Gayles (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Darrin P. Gayles, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Email proposed orders and jury instructions to the judge’s chambers address. Counsel can contact chambers about her procedures, hearing scheduling, or the status of pending matters, but not about rule-governed procedures.

docs.t: Judge Darrin P. Gayles (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Darrin P. Gayles, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: Counsel must appear in person for hearings on all substantive motions. With prior permission, counsel outside Miami-Dade and Broward can appear by phone for status conferences and calendar calls.

docs.t: Judge Darrin P. Gayles (S.D. Fla.) — Scheduling
docs.x: Judge Darrin P. Gayles, S.D. Fla.. Scheduling: After the defendants appear, file a joint scheduling report and a proposed scheduling order in her preferred format, and email the order in Word. The court won’t set a pretrial conference and sets trial after receiving them.

docs.t: Judge Darrin P. Gayles (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery and settlement
docs.x: Judge Darrin P. Gayles, S.D. Fla.. Discovery and settlement: The court refers all discovery matters to the magistrate judge. If a case settles, contact chambers immediately and file a notice of settlement.

docs.t: Judge David S. Leibowitz (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge David S. Leibowitz, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Email is the preferred method. Chambers won’t answer substantive questions or rule-governed ones, and every communication must copy all opposing counsel or pro se parties.

docs.t: Judge David S. Leibowitz (S.D. Fla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge David S. Leibowitz, S.D. Fla.. Proposed orders: As Local Rule 7.1(a)(2) requires, email a Word version of every proposed order to chambers after filing it on the docket.

docs.t: Judge David S. Leibowitz (S.D. Fla.) — Other
docs.x: Judge David S. Leibowitz, S.D. Fla.. Other: The page has a separate Criminal Procedures section, which we didn’t summarize.

docs.t: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg (S.D. Fla.) — Communications
docs.x: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg, S.D. Fla.. Communications: Any request for relief goes on the docket as a motion unless the rules allow otherwise. Don’t raise substantive matters by phone or email. Non-substantive calls and emails must follow the Federal and Local Rules.

docs.t: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: The court may set hearings on its own, other than for matters referred to the magistrate judge. They usually start at 8:30 a.m. and run 15 minutes unless the court allows more.

docs.t: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg (S.D. Fla.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg, S.D. Fla.. Trial: Calendar call is typically the Wednesday before the two-week trial period, and defendants aren’t transported for it. The order setting trial lists procedures she wants followed, and a sample is posted.

docs.t: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg (S.D. Fla.) — Criminal
docs.x: Judge Robin L. Rosenberg, S.D. Fla.. Criminal: The page also covers objections to presentence reports, which we didn’t summarize.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The chambers email address is the preferred way to reach chambers, and all emails must copy opposing counsel and pro se parties. For time-sensitive matters or emergencies you may call chambers, the courtroom deputy, or the law clerks about his specific procedures or to change a hearing because of unforeseen circumstances. Chambers won’t answer questions the Federal or Local Rules govern or give legal advice.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Scheduling report
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Scheduling report: Once a defendant appears, file a joint scheduling report and proposed scheduling order in his preferred format, and email the proposed order in Word to chambers. He sets trial after receiving them. The report must say what kind of trial you want, and a party demanding a jury must give the legal basis for the demand.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Mediation
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Mediation: By the date in his scheduling order, choose a mediator under Local Rule 16.2 and file a Notice of Mediator Selection and Hearing with a proposed Order Scheduling Mediation in his form, and email the Word version that day. Mediation is in person unless you move for good cause to hold it virtually before filing the notice.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Motions: Every motion, response, and reply is double-spaced in 12-point Times New Roman unless he orders otherwise. Multiple plaintiffs or defendants file joint motions unless their positions clearly conflict, and the page limits for individual parties apply to joint papers. Multiple defendants file one combined response or separate answers within the time for the last-served defendant.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings and trial
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Hearings and trial: Counsel must appear in person for hearings on all substantive motions, and may request phone or video by motion at least one day before. Calendar call is usually the Tuesday before the two-week trial period at 11:00 a.m., and he sets no pretrial conference unless the parties show good cause.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: He refers all discovery to the magistrate judge, so follow the paired magistrate judge’s discovery procedures to see whether written discovery motions are allowed. His page links procedures for Reinhart, Valle, Louis, McCabe, Strauss, and Maynard.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Settlement and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Settlement and proposed orders: If a case settles, call or email chambers right away and file a notice of settlement. Email every proposed order in Word. Anyone moving for unopposed relief must email a proposed order granting it the same day, and if no response is filed to a motion, submit a proposed order granting it within seven days after the response deadline passes.

docs.t: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz (S.D. Fla.) — Electronic equipment
docs.x: Judge Rodolfo Ruiz, S.D. Fla.. Electronic equipment: Move for permission to use electronic equipment at a hearing or trial, listing the items and who will use them. His page also posts a change of plea colloquy and sample scheduling, mediation, and jury trial orders.

docs.t: Judge Lisette M. Reid (S.D. Fla.) — Filings
docs.x: Judge Lisette M. Reid, S.D. Fla.. Filings: Follow the Local Rules for sealed filings. Email proposed orders to her chambers in Word format.

docs.t: Judge Lisette M. Reid (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Lisette M. Reid, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: When the district judge refers all discovery, she issues a standing discovery order with procedures for disputes. Written discovery motions need leave of court. Don’t wait until a month before the cutoff to start discovery, because lack of diligence isn’t good cause to extend it.

docs.t: Judge Lisette M. Reid (S.D. Fla.) — Advice
docs.x: Judge Lisette M. Reid, S.D. Fla.. Advice: The page encourages courtesy and the participation of lawyers with five years or less of experience in all proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Have the case number and presiding judge ready when you contact chambers.

docs.t: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: In referred cases, her Order Setting Discovery Procedures applies. She may also issue an Order Setting Discovery Status Conference, a phone conference about a month before the discovery deadline, but not in every case. Watch for case-specific orders on how to brief or set a dispute.

docs.t: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard (S.D. Fla.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Shaniek Mills Maynard, S.D. Fla.. Settlement: She has a standing order and checklist for settlement conferences. As a general rule she recuses from the case after conducting one, unless the parties file a notice waiving that so she can remain as the paired magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge Ellen Frances D'Angelo (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Ellen Frances D'Angelo, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Counsel can contact the deputy and law clerks about her procedures, but not substantive matters or rule-governed ones. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Email proposed orders to her chambers address.

docs.t: Judge Ellen Frances D'Angelo (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
