docs.t: Judge Marty Fulgueira Elfenbein (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Marty Fulgueira Elfenbein, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Counsel can contact chambers about her procedures and hearing scheduling, but not substantive or rule-governed questions. When you call, have all counsel of record on the line. Email proposed orders and scheduling matters to her chambers address.

docs.t: Judge Marty Fulgueira Elfenbein (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Marty Fulgueira Elfenbein, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: When all discovery is referred, she issues a standing discovery order. Written discovery motions need leave of court. Confer first, and if the court must step in, contact chambers to schedule a hearing. A personal conference, in person or by phone, is required unless the other side refuses, and then tell the court. Don’t call chambers for an immediate ruling during a deposition.

docs.t: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Counsel can contact chambers about her procedures, but chambers won’t give legal advice, and absent a true emergency counsel shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Copy all counsel on any email, except confidential statements for a settlement conference. Email proposed orders and scheduling matters to her chambers address.

docs.t: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: When all discovery is referred, she issues a standing discovery order. Written discovery motions need leave of court.

docs.t: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett (S.D. Fla.) — Courtroom
docs.x: Judge Enjoliqué A. Lett, S.D. Fla.. Courtroom: Test the courtroom equipment in advance by asking chambers to schedule it 24 hours before the hearing or trial.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Law clerks can answer procedural questions only. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Absent a true emergency, counsel of record shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Email his chambers address for proposed orders, jury instructions, and settlement conference memoranda.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Electronic equipment
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Electronic equipment: His chambers is electronics-friendly, but check with the clerk or the Marshals Service on courthouse rules for phones and devices. File a motion asking permission to use phones, laptops, or other electronics at a hearing or trial.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Arguing lawyers
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Arguing lawyers: Ordinarily one lawyer per party argues. Tell him before the hearing if a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, and multiple lawyers may. His order strongly encourages their participation in all proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: The order takes precedence over conflicting local procedures. You must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by Zoom, since email alone isn’t enough, and the motion must include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: File a discovery motion of no more than five pages that frames the issues, cites the best authority, and attaches the relevant requests and responses, described under CM/ECF procedure 3L(2). The response is due in five business days in five pages, and no reply is allowed. He then decides on a hearing. The parties may agree to extend interim discovery deadlines, such as response dates, without the court as long as the discovery cutoff and other scheduling order dates don’t change. He won’t take calls or attempts to get immediate rulings on deposition conduct, so proceed with the deposition and raise it by post-deposition motion. Keep trying to resolve it after a hearing is set and tell chambers promptly.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate or general objections, and vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless. Explain specifically and support burden with an affidavit. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness, say whether a request is irrelevant or disproportionate and why, confer to narrow scope, and produce the undisputed part. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing. Privilege objections must follow Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B) and include a log, or may be waived.

docs.t: Judge Raag Singhal (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Raag Singhal, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The only procedure posted on the judge’s page is the chambers email address for proposed orders and jury instructions. Check the court’s Local Rules and the orders in your case.

docs.t: Judge Rodney Smith (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Rodney Smith, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The only procedure posted on the judge’s page is the chambers email address for proposed orders and jury instructions. Check the court’s Local Rules and the orders in your case.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Kuntz (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Kuntz, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The only procedure posted on the judge’s page is the chambers email address for proposed orders and jury instructions. Check the court’s Local Rules and the orders in your case.

docs.t: Judge K. Michael Moore (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge K. Michael Moore, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The only procedure posted on the judge’s page is the chambers email address for proposed orders and jury instructions. Check the court’s Local Rules and the orders in your case.

docs.t: Judge Melissa Damian (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Melissa Damian, S.D. Fla.. Communication: The page gives a chambers email address and says that, absent the court’s permission, any correspondence to chambers must be copied to all counsel of record and pro se parties.

docs.t: Judge Aileen Cannon (S.D. Fla.) — Civil procedures
docs.x: Judge Aileen Cannon, S.D. Fla.. Civil procedures: The page posts only a Word exhibit list template and a trial plan template. We found no written standing procedures. Use the templates if you have a trial, and check the court’s orders in your case.

docs.t: Judge Jose E. Martinez (S.D. Fla.) — Communication and sentencing
docs.x: Judge Jose E. Martinez, S.D. Fla.. Communication and sentencing: The page gives an email address for proposed orders and jury instructions and links the judge’s Sentencing Procedures PDF. That PDF is for criminal cases, and we didn’t read it.

docs.t: Judge Joan A. Lenard (S.D. Fla.) — No contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Joan A. Lenard, S.D. Fla.. No contact with chambers: All inquiries and requests for relief, including scheduling and status requests, must be filed on the docket. Emails, calls, and any other contact with chambers or her law clerks are strictly prohibited without the court’s prior authorization. The only email address on the page is for proposed orders and jury instructions.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — No substantive discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. No substantive discovery motions: Don’t raise discovery disputes by Rule 37 motion, because substantive discovery motions on the docket are stricken and the local rule’s briefing provision doesn’t apply. The exception is a motion to stay discovery altogether, which goes to the district judge.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Weekly discovery calendar
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Weekly discovery calendar: He holds a discovery calendar every Thursday from 10:00 to 3:00 in Courtroom 5 at the King Federal Justice Building in Miami. After conferring with the other side on dates, call chambers by noon on the Friday before to get on that week’s calendar. He ordinarily allows 30 minutes per side.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Motion for Hearing and source materials
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Motion for Hearing and source materials: On the day he confirms your time, file a Motion for Hearing stating the date, the category of the discovery issues, the status of your pre-filing efforts, and a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate of conferral, or it can be denied. By noon on the Monday before the hearing, give him the source materials by hand or as a scanned PDF to his chambers mailbox, with a proposed order stating the specific relief for each request. Missing any of the three may cancel the hearing. Tell him promptly if you resolve or narrow the dispute. After the hearing, file a motion for entry of an amended proposed order within two business days.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: You must actually confer, and an adequate certificate almost always needs at least one personal communication, since unanswered emails aren’t enough. He deems an issue waived if you don’t confer or certify. He strictly enforces Local Rule 26.1(g)(2), reads the 28-day window as the time to make resolution efforts with only the seven-day agreed extension, and doesn’t recognize unapproved extensions. All discovery, including resolving disputes, must be done by the cutoff and he gives no remedy after it.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Privilege and burden
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Privilege and burden: The party with the burden on a privilege claim must present sworn evidence by the hearing, or the privilege may be deemed waived, and the evidence goes in the emailed materials and on the docket as a notice of filing. The objecting party carries the burden of showing specifically how a request is unreasonable, and failing that brings an order compelling and possible sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No conclusory boilerplate objections, and vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden may need sworn evidence. Relevance objections must explain why. Don’t recite an objection and then answer subject to it, which preserves nothing, and state that everything responsive was provided or describe what is withheld. Generalized privilege objections don’t comply with Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B). Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving, not filing, the objections, and he decides them only after the deposition.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Depositions and sequencing
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Depositions and sequencing: To object to deposition timing, serve a notice of objection within five days after receiving the notice, not on the eve, or the objection may be waived, then confer and use the discovery calendar if you can’t agree. Each party may sequence its own discovery under Rule 26(d)(3), and don’t wait until the end to take depositions, since failing to finish them isn’t good cause to extend discovery. He strictly enforces Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures and will compel supplemental depositions if they weren’t followed.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Applicable rules and unaccepted filings
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Applicable rules and unaccepted filings: Her Court Practices and Procedures for Civil Cases (last updated June 5, 2019) sits on top of the Federal and Local Rules. The court won’t accept notices of unavailability, notices of deposition, or other filings the rules don’t contemplate, and will strike them. A notice of unavailability doesn’t change the schedule.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Proposed orders: Email a Word version of every proposed order to chambers, as Local Rule 7.1(a)(2) requires. Proposed scheduling orders must follow her sample format and be emailed after they are filed.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Extensions: Deadlines are strict. Move for an extension at least 48 hours before the deadline unless there is an emergency, or risk sanctions. The motion must list prior extension motions and rulings, state the circumstances, include the Local Rule 7.1 conferral statement, and request a specific period. Indefinite requests are denied, and after a scheduling order extensions are disfavored.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Summary judgment: Follow Local Rule 56.1. The movant files a numbered statement of undisputed facts with record cites, and the opponent answers by corresponding number, saying disputed or undisputed and why a dispute is material. Facts the evidence supports are deemed admitted unless controverted.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Excess pages and sealing
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Excess pages and sealing: A motion for excess pages must say how many pages and why. A motion to seal must state the period to seal, indefinite sealing needs a substantial showing, and a proposed redacted version must accompany it and be filed publicly if the motion is granted.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Motions in limine: Each side may file one motion in limine, with up to ten numbered evidentiary issues, in no more than 20 pages. Confer on every issue first and certify it under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3), and raise only issues still contested. Responses and replies follow the movant’s order and numbering.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Pretrial filings: Use her witness list and exhibit list formats, list only witnesses you will actually call with a short synopsis, related exhibits, and time estimates, and tie each exhibit to a witness. Joint proposed jury instructions follow the Eleventh Circuit pattern, with plaintiff’s language underlined and defendant’s italicized, authority for every instruction, and emailed in Word. Joint deposition designations use color highlighting, with objections underlined in red and the basis in the margin.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Settlement: Tell the court immediately by call or email and file a joint stipulation of dismissal promptly. The court won’t retain jurisdiction over confidential settlements unless the terms are put on the record, and then only for a finite period.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Communications with chambers: Requests for relief go on the docket as motions. No substantive matters by phone or email, and no calls about anything the rules or docket answer. Letters aren’t accepted, and ex parte letters are put on the docket. Email subject lines must show the docket number, caption, and contents, and copy all counsel. Calls come only from counsel of record after conferring with all parties, with opposing counsel on the line, giving the docket number, caption, name, whether opposing counsel was consulted, and the reason.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Proposed orders: Email the final Word version of proposed orders and jury instructions to chambers under CM/ECF Administrative Procedure 3.I(6), with the case number and a short description in the subject line, copying all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Status report and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Status report and scheduling: The Notice of Status Conference requires a Joint Status Report, which satisfies Rule 16. After the status conference the court enters a scheduling order. Calendar every date.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Extensions: Motions to extend, continue, or enlarge are rarely granted. Each party gets one, and no second request after a grant. The caption must show the motions deadline, pretrial conference, calendar call, trial period, the number of prior extension requests, and whether the motion is referred to the magistrate judge, or it is summarily denied. Ask to extend discovery at least 10 days before the deadline, and the court generally won’t allow discovery past it, without changing other deadlines.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Form and conferral
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Form and conferral: Papers are one-sided, double-spaced, 12-point, with one-inch margins and page numbers at the bottom. Every motion needs a proposed order emailed separately in Word or WordPerfect with the docket entry in the subject line. State the other side’s position and describe your conferral efforts with dates under Local Rule 7.1.a.3, or expect denial.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Trial and mediation
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Trial and mediation: Be ready for the scheduled trial, because over 90 percent of cases are reached in the trial period. In consent cases put “CONSENT CASE” in bold under the case number. Use mediation early, and ask for a settlement conference before the magistrate judge at any time.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Pending motions
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Pending motions: If a ripe motion, or a decision after oral argument or a bench trial, is pending more than 45 days, contact chambers and tell the Judicial Administrator.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — What the page is
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. What the page is: It is a long “Friendly Random Advice for Litigants” guide, not a set of rules. It says to read the Local Rules and not to surprise the judge.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — Motions practice
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. Motions practice: Raise problems with opposing counsel and then the court as early as possible. State the issue and relief up front. Be brief, avoid acronyms, and use names, not pronouns. File summary judgment motions early, not at the deadline. Local Rule 7.1.C.2 bars multiple summary judgment motions, so get approval first for a successive one. File a reply or tell the court you won’t, or the court waits for the reply deadline and may take your silence as conceding points. Don’t adopt other filings by reference, and cite the record by page and line.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — Record and logistics
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. Record and logistics: Ask chambers whether the judge wants mini-script depositions or a separate courtesy set. Keep the record lean, and get approval before exceeding length limits. Test equipment for virtual hearings. Call chambers as soon as an issue is resolved or the case settles. Be careful with emergency motions, and never file one at 4:45 p.m. on a Friday.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Only counsel of record may contact chambers, and absent a true emergency not about the status of pending matters. Use of electronic devices in his hearings requires a motion.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — CM/ECF
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. CM/ECF: If personal information is filed by mistake, move to strike and file a redacted version. Non-trial exhibits may be attachments but must be labeled by content, not just a number or letter, and documents with several attachments need PDF bookmarks. Proposed orders go in as an attachment and by email in an editable format, preferably Word.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Civil practice
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Civil practice: He generally issues a standard pretrial scheduling order and holds pretrial conferences, Daubert hearings (the challenged expert must attend), and motions in limine hearings. He has no extra rules for extensions, continuances, or ex parte restraining orders. He hears preliminary injunction motions and takes evidence. Telephone hearings and oral argument are allowed on advance request for good cause. Don’t send copies of published cases.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery and settlement
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Discovery and settlement: He generally issues an order setting discovery deadlines and procedures. Don’t call chambers for an immediate ruling during a deposition. Mediation is required in all cases, and counsel submit a proposed referral order. Tell chambers immediately of a settlement and file a notice.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Trial: He sets trial dates after conferring with lead counsel and requires trial briefs in bench trials. Counsel conduct voir dire, peremptory strikes alternate, and back striking isn’t allowed. He may limit opening statements, requires advance approval for demonstratives in them, and bars plaintiff rebuttal in openings. No speaking objections. Proposed jury instructions go in electronically, and in bench trials proposed findings are filed electronically.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Email proposed orders, jury instructions, and other filings the court directs to her chambers address, and copy all counsel and pro se parties except on confidential statements. Her page also gives telephonic hearing dial-in instructions.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Protective orders
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Protective orders: A stipulation to keep discovery confidential isn’t a court order. File a joint motion for a Rule 26(c) protective order and send the proposed order in Word to chambers. She omits any provision that would bypass Local Rule 5.4’s sealing requirements.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate objections. Say specifically how a request is vague, overbroad, unduly burdensome, irrelevant, or disproportionate, and ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. “Not reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence” is outdated. If you object to scope, produce what isn’t disputed. State what you’re withholding. Providing discovery “subject to and without waiving” an objection is improper and the objection is waived. Blanket privilege objections need a privilege log or may be deemed waived, and production of nonprivileged material can’t wait for the log. Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving objections before the deposition, not by moving for a protective order. The objector carries the burden, and failure shifts fees under Rule 37.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Timing and conferral
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Timing and conferral: Raise discovery disputes within Local Rule 26.1(g)(2)’s time, which she strictly enforces. All discovery, including resolving disputes, must be done by the cutoff, and she offers no remedy after it, even by agreement. Before raising a dispute, confer by live conversation, since email alone isn’t enough, and certify the dates and means under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3). Failing to confer can alone justify denial, and the other side’s failure counts against it on fees.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Two ways to raise a dispute
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Two ways to raise a dispute: You may file a written discovery motion without leave, limited to ten pages for the motion and response and five for a reply, and a hearing isn’t guaranteed. Or use her Informal Discovery Hearing procedure, which isn’t mandatory and can’t decide sanctions motions but can decide a Rule 37(a) motion to compel.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Informal discovery hearing
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Informal discovery hearing: Confer and identify at least two dates within the next 14 days. The movant sends one email to chambers copying all parties, with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing,” the case number and caption, the proposed dates, the expected length, and a certification of conferral. After she confirms, file a Notice of Hearing within 24 hours (two business days for a pro se movant) describing each dispute in two or three sentences without argument, or it is stricken. By noon two business days before, each party emails the relevant source materials, separately and with descriptive titles, and a proposed order stating the specific relief for each request.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Law clerks can answer procedural questions, not substantive or strategy questions. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Absent a true emergency, counsel of record shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Telephonic hearing dial-in instructions are on his page.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Electronic equipment
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Electronic equipment: To bring audio or video equipment into the courtroom, comply with Administrative Order 2018-79 and file the motion at least 48 hours ahead. He posts a sample order.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: He is guided by his Standing Discovery Order, the Florida Bar guidelines for professional conduct, and the Chief Justice’s 2015 Year-End Report. His page also posts an Order Setting Discovery Status Conference, his best-practices article, a discovery remedies chart, Rule 502(d) clawback order forms, and confidentiality order forms.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: Ordinarily only one lawyer per party may argue. If a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, tell the court before the hearing starts and multiple lawyers may argue for that party.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Standing Discovery Order (January 2024)
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Standing Discovery Order (January 2024): The order applies to discovery in his cases and sanctions can follow noncompliance. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. Responding doesn’t waive objections to future requests. If parties can’t agree on a deposition date after conferring, the requesting party may set it with Local Rule 26.1(h) notice and the deponent must move for a protective order. He won’t rule on ESI search disputes in advance: the responding party searches and the requester can challenge whether the inquiry was reasonable. Instructions that impose duties beyond the rules have no effect. A response promising production at an indeterminate time is unacceptable, so give a completion date, and a final production date more than 30 days after the response deadline is presumptively unreasonable. A protective-order

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery objections
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery objections: No boilerplate or general objections, and the court strikes them. Say whether responsive material is being withheld, and a later claim that no documents exist after an objection draws sanctions. Ask for clarification before objecting that a term is vague, and otherwise define the term yourself and respond. Overbroad is ambiguous, so say whether you mean irrelevant or disproportionate. Confer to narrow scope, and answer the undisputed part. “Subject to and without waiving” objections are barred, and for interrogatories an objection plus an answer waives the objection. “To the extent that” objections are inadequate. Privilege objections need the specifics and a log, or they may be waived. Privilege at a deposition is raised question by question. For a Rule 30(b)(6) notice he typically won’t rule on objections in advance, and the dep

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery disputes: You must actually speak with opposing counsel, in person or by phone. Don’t file a discovery motion first. The movant emails chambers with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing,” offering two afternoons within the next seven business days, the time needed, and a certification of conferral, copying all counsel. He sets the hearing by order and counsel appear in person. At least 48 hours before, file a joint discovery memorandum of five pages or less describing the dispute, certifying conferral, and attaching the source materials, in his sample format. If it isn’t resolved he may authorize a motion, which then triggers Rule 37(a)(5) fees.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Objections: An objection that a request isn’t reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence is outdated and meritless on its own. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. No generalized, vague, or boilerplate objections. “Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome” alone is meaningless and stricken. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. “Overbroad” alone is inadequate, so say whether you mean irrelevant or disproportionate and why. Confer to narrow scope, answer the undisputed part, and support a burden claim with an affidavit. Unless impractical, support a burden objection to ESI search terms with evidence of the expected number of hits.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: Counsel must actually speak, in person or by phone. Email or text isn’t enough, and you should discuss every request and objection at issue. Seek court help within 28 days of when the grounds arise under Local Rule 26.1(g)(2)(A), and at least seven days before the discovery cutoff absent exceptional circumstances, or the relief can be denied automatically. Conferring before objections doesn’t excuse conferring again before requesting a hearing.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — No written discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. No written discovery motions: Don’t file written discovery motions between parties unless an order authorizes it. This covers any Rule 26 or Rule 37 motion, including to compel, for a protective order, for discovery sanctions, to strike an untimely expert, and to extend time to respond to discovery, though he expects you to agree to reasonable extensions. The exception is a dispute with a non-party, which can be raised by motion of five double-spaced pages with no reply, and you must give the non-party a copy of his procedures.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Notice of Discovery Dispute
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Notice of Discovery Dispute: To get a hearing, file a Notice of Discovery Dispute, not a motion, after conferring on every issue. It describes the dispute in one or two sentences, states the discovery deadline and your conferral efforts, offers at least three alternative dates within two weeks with morning, afternoon, or all-day availability, gives the time needed, and certifies conferral. No argument, and the opposing party doesn’t respond. If the other side completely failed to respond by a firm deadline, file a Notice of Complete Failure to Respond to Discovery with three dates, and he cancels the hearing if the discovery is produced.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Joint discovery status report
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Joint discovery status report: At least 48 hours before the hearing, file a joint report and email a Word copy. For each dispute, give the verbatim request and response, a succinct statement of each side’s position, and the result of conferral, in his chart, with the combined positions on one page per request. Keep trying to resolve or narrow the dispute and tell chambers promptly if you do.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Fees and hearings
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Fees and hearings: He treats arguments at the hearing as oral motions to compel or for a protective order and requires the loser to pay fees under Rule 37(a)(5) where warranted, and may impose other sanctions. Ordinarily one lawyer per party argues, but if a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, tell him beforehand and multiple lawyers may argue.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Stipulated orders
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Stipulated orders: File a joint motion attaching the proposed order, then immediately email a Word copy to his chambers address.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Communication and equipment
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Communication and equipment: Law clerks can answer procedural questions only. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Absent a true emergency, counsel of record shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Motions to bring electronic equipment into court are due at least 72 hours before the hearing or trial, under Administrative Order 2018-79.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Arguing lawyers
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Arguing lawyers: Ordinarily one attorney per party argues, but if you tell the court before the hearing that a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, multiple attorneys may.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: Counsel must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by video. Email or a voicemail alone isn’t enough. Keep trying after a hearing is set, and tell chambers promptly if issues resolve.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Scheduling a hearing
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Scheduling a hearing: After conferring, call chambers to get available dates, confirm them with opposing counsel, and call back to finalize. Make multiple attempts to reach opposing counsel, and if there is no response in three business days you may finalize a date that fits your own schedule. Continuing that hearing then takes a motion showing good cause with three alternative dates. The first discovery hearing is typically by Zoom unless you request otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: The same day you finalize the hearing, file a concise discovery motion of no more than three pages, with the specific substance, the best authority, a conferral certification, and the source materials attached. Only one per hearing without authorization. The response is due within two business days in three pages, and a reply within one business day in two pages. Don’t spend space on background, make your arguments in the briefing, and don’t incorporate conferral letters or emails by reference. She may rule without a hearing. Disputed discovery motions that skip these steps are denied, though joint motions for stipulated orders are fine.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Objections: Not reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence is outdated and meritless. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. No boilerplate or general objections. Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden needs an affidavit or similar statement. Seek clarification before objecting to vagueness and confer to narrow scope, then provide the undisputed discovery. An objection followed by an answer subject to or without waiving it preserves nothing. Privilege objections must follow Local Rule 26.1(e)(2), and a missing privilege log can waive the objection.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Scope: His procedures apply to all civil cases assigned or referred to him and take precedence over the local rules’ procedures under Local Rule 26.1(g)(1). If the district judge’s order conflicts, for example by barring discovery motions, and no order says how to submit a dispute, email chambers asking for instructions with the subject “Request re: Submission of Discovery Dispute in [Case Number]” and don’t describe the dispute.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: Counsel must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by Zoom. Email alone isn’t enough. Discuss options and make a concerted good-faith effort, and include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate in the motion.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: File a discovery motion of no more than five pages that frames the issues, cites the best authority, and attaches the relevant requests and responses, described under CM/ECF procedure 3L(2). The response is due within five business days in five pages, and no reply is allowed. He then decides whether a hearing is needed.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — After a hearing is set
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. After a hearing is set: Keep trying to resolve it and email chambers promptly to cancel or narrow the hearing, copying all counsel and giving no argument or background in the email.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate or general objections. Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden may need an affidavit. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. Say whether a request is irrelevant or disproportionate and why. Confer to narrow scope, and produce the undisputed part. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing. State that everything responsive has been produced or describe what you’re withholding. Privilege objections need the specifics and a log, or may be waived.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Motion for Discovery Hearing
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Motion for Discovery Hearing: After conferring under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3), file a “Motion for Discovery Hearing,” and no other discovery motion or memorandum without her permission. It may contain only: a short statement of the disputed issues and relief sought, a list of documents you’ll rely on at the hearing (not discovery materials), a list of legal authorities with a parenthetical for each and which issue it applies to but no argument, any time constraints, at least three Tuesday-through-Friday dates within 14 days when the parties are available (or simply say they couldn’t agree), any request to file a formal motion or memorandum, and a certificate of conferral. No exhibits or conferral emails. Noncompliant motions and responses may be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Response and email to chambers
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Response and email to chambers: The opposing party responds within three days with only the same items and no argument or exhibits, and no replies without leave. After filing, email the motion or response to her discovery address with the subject “Discovery Dispute” or “Response to Discovery Dispute,” the case number and name, and a one-sentence body in her form. Attach a proposed order (Word, 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, justified, page-numbered after page one) and highlighted source materials, attaching only the responses if they’ve been filed. Conferral emails aren’t source material.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: She sets hearings in person in Fort Lauderdale, and grants a Zoom request if the lawyer arguing is outside the district. A motion to continue needs three alternative Tuesday-through-Friday dates. To bring a laptop or other equipment, file a short motion at least 24 hours before saying who and what. Present exhibits by Zoom screen share. She encourages less-experienced lawyers to argue.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Timing
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Timing: Raise disputes as Local Rule 26.1(g)(2) requires, and finish all discovery, including disputes, before the cutoff under Rule 26.1(d). She enforces both.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Other: A stipulation isn’t a court order, so move for a Rule 26(c) protective order and email the Word version, and she omits any provision that would bypass Local Rule 5.4’s sealing rules. Seek sanctions by separate motion. A pending motion to stay discovery doesn’t excuse responding to discovery.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers email
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Chambers email: Her page gives one address for proposed orders, jury instructions and other filings the court directs, and a separate address for discovery matters under her procedures.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: Confer in person, by video, or by phone, since email alone isn’t enough, and certify it under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3). She strictly enforces Local Rule 26.1(g)(2) and reads the 28-day window as the time to make good-faith resolution efforts, with the seven-day extension under 26.1(g)(2)(C) only, and won’t recognize extensions the parties agree to without approval. All discovery, including disputes, must be finished before the cutoff and no remedy is available after it.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — No discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. No discovery motions: Don’t raise discovery disputes by Rule 37 motion without leave, because they’ll be stricken. The restriction doesn’t apply to motions to stay discovery or to extend the time to respond to discovery, which go to the district judge.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Setting a hearing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Setting a hearing: Email her chambers within the Rule 26.1(g)(2) time, copying opposing counsel, with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing on [Case Number and Case Name],” at least three dates in the next ten days showing morning, afternoon, or all-day availability, and no argument. She ordinarily allows 30 minutes per side, and you must state if you need more. The hearings aren’t informal, so be fully prepared.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Notice of Hearing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Notice of Hearing: Within one business day of her confirming the date, file a Notice of Hearing of no more than five pages per side outlining each issue and each side’s position, without argument. Attach a short proposed order, all relevant source materials, and a list of the legal authorities with copies (highlighting and parentheticals allowed but no argument), and include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate. Nothing more can be submitted without leave. Don’t file conferral emails, which she doesn’t accept as evidence of conferral. Notify chambers and file a Notice of Cancellation if you resolve everything.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Agreed orders
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Agreed orders: Don’t move for an agreed order. Email chambers the proposed order in Word with a statement that the parties agree. She doesn’t enter stipulated orders extending the time to respond to discovery or memorializing discovery agreements that weren’t litigated.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Objections: Blanket vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome objections are meaningless, and you may need sworn evidence of burden. Seek clarification before objecting to vagueness. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing, so say that everything responsive was provided or describe what is withheld. Privilege objections need the Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B) details and a log, and the party with the burden must file any sworn evidence as an exhibit to the Notice of Hearing or may waive the privilege. Produce the undisputed part when objecting on scope. Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving, not filing, the objections before the deposition, and she decides them only after it.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Sequencing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Sequencing: Each party may sequence its own discovery under Rule 26(d)(3), so one side’s discovery doesn’t make the other wait. Don’t leave depositions to the end, because failing to finish them before the cutoff isn’t good cause to extend it.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Berger (M.D. Fla.) — AI certification (standing order, April 2, 2026)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Berger, M.D. Fla.. AI certification (standing order, April 2, 2026): Every filing, by counsel or pro se, must end with a certification: either that no generative AI was used in drafting and preparing it, or that any AI-drafted language (even if later edited) was personally reviewed by a human for accuracy and every citation is to a real authority that says what you claim. The certification does not count against page limits. Non-compliant filings may be stricken without consideration and without leave to amend. Repeated failures can bring sanctions up to dismissal with prejudice, default, and a bar referral.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Berger (M.D. Fla.) — Other standing order and preferences
docs.x: Judge Wendy Berger, M.D. Fla.. Other standing order and preferences: Her page also posts a Standing Order on Revised Local Rules (January 2021), which we have not read. Criminal: the government must file a notice of the maximum penalty for each count within 14 days after the charge is docketed. Civil forms: her own patent case management report, exhibit certification form, and exhibit labels and list.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn Kimball Mizelle (M.D. Fla.) — Posted forms
docs.x: Judge Kathryn Kimball Mizelle, M.D. Fla.. Posted forms: Her page posts no standing orders or preferences. It posts her own Certificate of Interested Persons and Corporate Disclosure Statement form, a patent case management report, and exhibit labels and list forms, in addition to the court’s uniform case management report and criminal disclosure statement.

docs.t: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez (D. Colo.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez, D. Colo.. Scope: Judges Rodriguez, Sweeney, Wang, Gallagher, and Crews share one set of Uniform Civil Practice Standards, effective December 9, 2025, with a judge’s initials marking any variation. Failing to follow them, the Local Rules, or the Federal Rules can get a filing struck without substantive consideration.

docs.t: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez (D. Colo.) — Extensions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez, D. Colo.. Extensions and continuances: Ask for an extension by written motion as far ahead as possible, showing particular good cause. The press of business typically isn’t good cause, and a motion filed after the original deadline won’t be considered. Note service on the client in the certificate of service, naming who received it. Ask for a continuance by written motion too. Oral motions on the day of a hearing or trial aren’t entertained, a stipulated continuance isn’t effective until the court approves it, and you should email chambers when you file.

docs.t: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez (D. Colo.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez, D. Colo.. Motions generally: Motion and argument go in one document, since a separately filed brief is noncompliant. Send a Word proposed order by email with any joint or unopposed motion. Exhibits are separate attachments labeled by number and name. Email chambers when you file an emergency motion. Separate requests for different actions need separate motions, and a request for action can’t be buried in a response or reply. Untimely or noncompliant papers may be denied or stricken on the court’s own motion. For Judge Rodriguez, supporting exhibits go in one consecutively numbered appendix, and a respondent adds its own.

docs.t: Judge Regina M. Rodriguez (D. Colo.) — Motions to dismiss and Rule 702
